instructions:
Elite Dangerous ship-build optimiser built on the Coriolis (coriolis.io) calculation engine and data.
Every number comes from the engine and documented game mechanics, never from community tier lists. Workflow:
1. Translate the user's goal into ONE objective metric plus hard constraints (list_metrics shows them).
   E.g. "best exploration Krait" -> objective unladenRange, constraints count:fs>=1, count:am>=1, count:pv>=1.
   "Tanky PvE FdL" -> objective totalEHP with constraint dpsVsHull>=X; "max cargo T-9 that can still jump 20 Ly laden" -> cargoCapacity, ladenRange>=20.
2. Required modules are constraints on count:<group> (list_module_groups gives group codes: fs fuel scoop, am AFMU, pv SRV hangar,
   fh fighter hangar, dc docking computer, hs heat sink, rf refinery, cc collector limpets, ml mining laser, ...).
3. Use compare_ships to rank hulls (effort quick, sizes to restrict), then optimize_build on the best few with effort normal/thorough.
4. Improving a player's build (pass it as "build"):
   - Lock every slot the request does not touch (lock: ["hardpoint", "standard:fsd", "internal:3", ...]).
   - Turn what the build already achieves into constraints (current shieldEHP, hullEHP, sustainedDps, unladenRange, ...
     as minimums) so the result is never worse where the player did not ask for a trade.
   - Ties keep the player's modules (keepBase), but a metric that genuinely improves will still swap modules:
     check the changed slots and explain each one.
5. Keep builds playable: one weapon type and mount type where possible (weaponTypes, mountTypes), a real fuel tank,
   no large fuel scoop on combat ships, required utility modules as count: constraints.
6. Ask how the player flies when it matters and set context: sysPips/wepPips while fighting (default 2/4),
   recoverySysPips (default 4), damagePreset pve for NPC combat, incomingDps, rangeMeters, opponent.
7. Present the Coriolis and EDSY links and explain trade-offs with the numbers. Users may paste builds from Coriolis,
   EDSY (SLEF export or import link), Inara or their journal; export_build gives SLEF / journal JSON.
8. Explore trade-offs by re-running with tightened constraints (epsilon-constraint method) rather than inventing weights.
Assumptions (say so when a result depends on them, and offer a rerun with another value): the pve damage mix,
regenUnderFire=0, thermalVentFactor=1 (Thermal Vent heat removal is unmeasured), Corrosive Shell 1.25x hull damage and
+20 piercing (community figures), engineering at best roll.
Engineering defaults to grade 5 best-roll blueprints plus the best experimental effect per module ("engineering":"none" for stock).
Guardian modules cannot be engineered; life support, sensors and SCO FSDs keep their slot size; all modules count as obtainable.
Searched module groups are limited to those that can affect the requested metrics; use extraGroups or count:<group> constraints to bring others in.
Optimisation is a heuristic local search: very good but not a proof of global optimality; higher effort = more restarts.
When the user asks about updates, use check_for_updates; install_update only after the user agrees.

tools.name: list_ships
tools.title: List ships
tools.description: All ships with id, size class (1 small - 3 large), price, base speed/boost, mass, masslock and slot layout.

tools.name: ship_details
tools.title: Ship details
tools.description: Slot keys/sizes/restrictions of a ship plus its full stock (or given) build summary. Slot keys are what lock/changes refer to.

build.description: A build in any common form: Coriolis outfit or import link, EDSY import link, SLEF JSON (EDSY: Export → SLEF), or a journal Loadout event.

sysPips.description: SYS pips while fighting: shield resistance, regen under fire (default 2)

wepPips.description: WEP pips while fighting: weapon capacitor sustain (default 4)

recoverySysPips.description: SYS pips while recovering: shield recharge and rebuild times (default 4)

damage.description: Incoming damage mix for effective-HP metrics (relative weights; default equal kinetic/thermal/explosive)

opponent.description: Reference target for dpsVsShields/dpsVsHull: ship id (stock) or any build (link, SLEF). Default stock Anaconda

damagePreset.description: Named damage mix: even (default) or pve (thermal-heavy NPC fire: K 0.30 / T 0.60 / E 0.05 / Abs 0.05, an assumption). Explicit damage weights override it.

regenUnderFire.description: Share of time shields regenerate while taking fire (default 0; the in-game pause after a hit is unmeasured)

ventHitRate.description: Share of time Thermal Vent beams are on target (default 1)

thermalVentFactor.description: Heat a hitting Thermal Vent beam removes, as a multiple of its own thermal load (default 1; unmeasured)

corrosiveHullMultiplier.description: Hull damage multiplier while a Corrosive Shell weapon keeps hitting (default 1.25; community figure, does not stack)

corrosivePiercingBonus.description: Armour piercing added to the Corrosive Shell weapon itself (default 20; community figure)

reserveFuelInJumpMass.description: Count the reserve tank in jump mass like Coriolis (default false, matching the journal MaxJumpRange)

tools.name: list_module_groups
tools.title: List module groups
tools.description: Module group codes (used in count:<group> metrics, extraGroups, filters) with names and categories.

tools.name: module_info
tools.title: Module info
tools.description: Stock stats of every module in a group (optionally one class) and the blueprints / experimental effects that apply to it, with grade-5 feature ranges.

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.title: List metrics
tools.description: Every metric usable as objective/constraint, with unit and meaning. Also: count:<group> and class:<group>.

tools.name: evaluate_build
tools.title: Evaluate build
tools.description: Full stats of a build (Coriolis URL or stock ship), optionally after applying slot changes. Use for what-if comparisons; returns a new Coriolis URL.

slot.description: Slot key from ship_details, e.g. internal:3, hardpoint:1, utility:2, standard:fsd, bulkheads

blueprint.description: Blueprint key, e.g. FSD_LongRange (module_info lists them)

tools.name: export_build
tools.title: Export build
tools.description: A build as SLEF (EDCD Ship Loadout Exchange Format, accepted by EDSY, Coriolis, Inara, EDDiscovery) or as a Frontier journal Loadout event, plus Coriolis and EDSY links.

build.description: A build in any common form: Coriolis outfit or import link, EDSY import link, SLEF JSON (EDSY: Export → SLEF), or a journal Loadout event.

tools.name: optimize_build
tools.title: Optimise build
tools.description: Search for the outfitting of one ship that maximises/minimises an objective metric subject to constraints, using the Coriolis engine for every evaluation. Starts from stock or a given build; lock keeps slots unchanged.

build.description: A build in any common form: Coriolis outfit or import link, EDSY import link, SLEF JSON (EDSY: Export → SLEF), or a journal Loadout event. Optimisation starts from it; locked slots keep its modules.

lock.description: Slot keys or kinds to keep: e.g. ["hardpoint","utility:1","standard:fsd"]

keepBase.description: On equal scores keep the starting build's modules instead of the cheaper fit (default true when build is given)

metric.description: Metric name from list_metrics, or count:<group> / class:<group>

direction.description: Defaults to the metric's natural direction

tiebreakers.description: Secondary goals used only to break exact ties

direction.description: Defaults to the metric's natural direction

engineering.description: full = G5 max roll + best experimental (default); none = stock modules

power.description: Power budget check. priority (default): combat modules powered with hardpoints out, non-combat ones (scoop, docking computer, SRV bay, ...) shed by priority as in game, everything powered with hardpoints retracted. deployed: everything on with hardpoints out.

requireBoost.description: Distributor must be able to boost (default true)

extraGroups.description: Extra module groups to consider even if no metric needs them

tools.name: check_for_updates
tools.title: Check for updates
tools.description: Installed corai version, the Coriolis code and data it was built from, and the latest corai release on GitHub with its notes.

tools.name: install_update
tools.title: Install update
tools.description: Updates this ED Corai install (a clean git clone) to a release: fetches the tag, refreshes the Coriolis submodules, installs dependencies and rebuilds. Only call after the user explicitly agreed. The MCP server must be restarted afterwards (Claude Code: /mcp, Claude Desktop: restart the app).

version.description: Release tag, e.g. "v0.2.0". Default: the latest release.

confirm.description: Must be true: the user agreed to install the update.
